decisions.executionNote: Bend both arms gradually into elbow-up overhead approaches in their respective workspaces; initial downward orientation is staged conservatively.
Finish vertical wrist alignment while approaching the outer left red disk and right blue block, keeping grippers open above them.
Correct visual centering using the lower tabletop estimate, descend to piece height, and close both grippers. Retention will be checked by lifting.
Lift both pieces to verify retention, then carry them inward above the board without crossing arms.
Align retained red disk with the tall left peg and blue block with the short right peg, then approach slowly for visual insertion checks.
Lower both retained pieces toward their peg bases in small vertical increments; watch for alignment or contact rather than assuming insertion.
Pieces show contact and slight tilt. Relieve vertical loading, correct a small fore-aft offset, and open to let the peg-guided pieces settle before inspecting.
Withdraw open grippers vertically and allow the tilted pieces to settle. Placement is not yet confirmed; reassess unobstructed peg and hole alignment.
Recover the perched red disk with a fresh grasp. Move the right arm to the isolated star, leaving the displaced blue block for later recovery.
Move the recovered red disk clear to expose its peg for visual alignment. Correct right-star centering from the wrist image and grasp it.
Use the exposed peg tip to approach red-hole alignment. Reopen and correct the star grasp fore-aft; the prior closure did not visibly retain it.
Refine red alignment from the peg's observed motion, then descend slowly. Lift the newly grasped star and begin carrying it toward the right-side pegs.
Make a small fore-aft correction on the red disk near the peg tip; carry the retained star above its right-side peg with clearance.
Relieve red contact and shift slightly toward the peg axis before a small descent. Center the star laterally and lower toward its peg while maintaining both grasps.
Red retention was lost. Withdraw the left arm to clear the center; move the single star to the short rightmost peg, avoiding simultaneous adjacent-arm insertion.
With the left arm clear, correct the star's held offset and descend gently toward the shortest peg, stopping above the base to check the hole.
The short peg is visible at the star hole. Continue a millimeter-scale insertion with a small fore-aft correction, holding before release.
The star now visibly surrounds the short peg. Open and withdraw the right gripper while approaching the nearest loose red disk with the left arm.
Star remains on the rightmost peg with gripper open. Clear the right arm and visually center, lower, and grasp the nearest red disk.
Lift the flat, centered red disk above the tall peg and transfer over its axis; keep the other arm well clear during insertion.
Compensate the held disk's observed offset and descend toward the tall peg in small increments, with the right arm stationary and clear.
The peg is visible through the red hole. Make a gentle short descent, release, and withdraw to see whether the disk settles onto the base.
The red disk did not settle on the peg. Approach the displaced disk for a centered regrasp; use the exposed peg-tip image to correct the next insertion rather than pressing.
Descend straight onto the visually centered red disk, close, and perform a short retention lift without contacting the neighboring pieces.
The prior closure missed the disk. Reopen, correct the fore-aft error at grasp height, and test a centered regrasp with a very short lift.
The red disk is now retained. Lift fully clear and realign above the tall peg, compensating its fore-aft grasp offset before another controlled insertion.
The disk hangs tilted in the grasp. Adjust wrist pitch gradually around the held piece, compensating link6 translation so the hole remains near the peg axis.
Bring the leveled red disk toward peg-tip height, adding a small rearward alignment correction and monitoring for contact.
Maintain the leveled grasp and test the next 20 mm of vertical insertion in millimeter increments; do not release until the peg is visibly threaded.
Apply a 3 mm fore-aft correction while continuing a shallow insertion, keeping the disk level and the other arm clear.
The peg now visibly passes through the red hole. Lower a short distance, release for gravity-assisted seating, and withdraw vertically.
The first red disk is seated around its peg. Clear it and approach the next nearby red disk with the proven wrist orientation, accounting for the link6-to-grasp offset.
Center the next red disk between the jaws using the wrist view, close at piece height, and perform a short lift to verify retention.
Reopen and advance the jaws slightly farther over the red disk before closing; retention was not evident in the prior attempt.
Return to a vertical pickup orientation and realign link6 over the disk, compensating the tilted tool offset. Inspect the open-jaw alignment before closing.
Fine-center the red disk within the open jaws at pickup height, close, and lift vertically to verify retention.
The next disk is securely retained and flatter. Lift over the tall peg, compensate the grasp offset, and approach above the first seated disk.
Lower the second red disk toward the exposed peg tip, preserving its grasp and checking for visible threading before release.
The peg is visibly threaded through the second red disk. Seat it gently, open the jaws, and withdraw to verify stacking.
Clear the left arm and allow the released disk to settle. Approach the central blue piece with the right arm, keeping both arms in their own workspaces.
Approach the central blue piece at pickup height without crossing the midline, then inspect centering before grasping.
Fine-center the blue block, close the gripper, and lift straight up to verify retention before transfer to its peg.
The blue block is retained. Carry it above the third peg, preserving its orientation and accounting for its fore-aft grasp offset.
Lower the retained blue block gently toward the third peg while preserving lateral alignment; inspect the hole before any release.
The peg tip is visible at the blue hole's upper-right edge. Apply a millimeter-scale centering correction and continue a shallow insertion before releasing.
The blue hole visibly surrounds the peg. Lower a short distance, open to allow seating, and withdraw without lateral motion.
Withdraw from the first blue block with reduced jaw opening to avoid neighboring pieces, then approach the second blue block at the board's right edge.
Center the second blue block and descend to pickup height with a narrower opening to avoid the adjacent star; close for a retention test.
Lift the second blue piece clear of neighboring toys, verify retention, and carry it above the third peg with its grasp offset compensated.
Correct the second blue block's lateral offset from the visible stack axis and descend slowly toward peg-tip height, keeping the grasp closed.
Continue the second blue block's shallow insertion with a 2 mm fore-aft correction toward the visible peg tip; maintain the grasp until threading is clear.
The second blue hole visibly surrounds the peg. Seat a few millimeters, release with limited jaw opening, and lift straight away to inspect both blue pieces.
Both blue pieces are not seated correctly after release. Regrasp the perched block over the third peg for a fore-aft alignment correction, without disturbing the star.
The jaws closed above the perched blue block. Reopen and descend to its actual grasp height, then close and make a short retention lift.
Correct the missed blue grasp toward the piece's near edge and lower to its sidewall height. Close and test retention with a small lift.
Use the observed wrist-image motion to bring the blue block farther between the open finger pads, with a small height reduction, then close without pulling on it.
The blue piece remains ahead of the finger pads. Reopen and shift the grasp farther over it while maintaining height, then close for another visual retention check.
The blue block is lower than the previous grasp attempts. Descend to tabletop pickup height with a small fore-aft correction, close, and make a short retention lift.
The blue block is now retained low between the pads. Lift clear and align its hole over the third peg using the newly observed grasp offset.
Lower the retained blue piece toward the third peg while preserving its measured grasp offset. Keep the jaws closed until it is fully threaded and seated.
